The knife roller (cutting roller) with through-out-devices for short cutting length of e.g. 4 mm. A roving feeding bar with doubled roving tube holes enables maximum input of up to 28 rovings. The front view of cutter WRC-400 illustrates the main drive, frequency controlled, powering the rubber roller (polyurethane roller), drive of oscillating unit for maximum life time of knives and rubber roller. Pneumatic cylinders were used for generating the necessary pressure between the rollers. This unit is being delivered to the Manufacturing Demonstration Facility (MDF) by early January 2022 and then installed/commissioned. At the time of writing this report, no cutting data is available for this cutter. Glass, TCF and basalt fiber will be used in the WRC- 400 which will enable comparison to the data provided in this report. The roving cutter enables cutting glass, carbon and basalt fibers of ½” and greater. Figures 6 and 7 provide a detailed view of the elements of the WRC-400 and how they are assembled with respect 8 to each other, namely – roving brake, deionization bar, oscillation unit with roving feeding bar, scraper device, pressure roller, cutter roller, contact roller, blow out device for contact roller and piker roller respectively. Figure 6 Cutter roller and contact roller shown in assembly Figure 7 Detailed view of the WR-400 Schmitz & Heinsman cutter procured and under installation (Feb 2022) 9 IACMI SMC – V1 The IACMI SMC line was designed to be 18” width to provide intermediate scale capability. It is known that industrial lines (at Polynt, AOC, Ineos, Owens Corning) range from 36” and greater width(s). The work done hence had to be scale-able to industrial lines. The cutting modules were designed to be readily replaced from one to the other depending upon the fibers being cut, i.e., glass, carbon, basalt etc. The resin systems to run on the line are flexible, i.e. polyester, vinyl ester, epoxy etc. Figure 8 illustrates the cutting module for the glass and basalt fiber rovings.
